body.note: From the English Magazine of Art
body.head: AFTER TWENTY YEARS.

lg.l:
DOWN on the ancient wharf, the sand, I sit, with a new-
comernew
comer chatting:

He shipp'd as green-hand boy, and sail'd away, (took some
sudden, vehement notion;)
Since, twenty years and more have circled round and round,

While he the globe was circling round and round,—and now
returns:

How changed the place—all the old land-marks gone—the
parents dead;

(Yes, he comes back to lay in post for good—to settle—has
a well-fill'd purse —no spot will do but this;

The little boat that scull'd him from the sloop, now held
in leash I see,

I hear the slapping waves, the restless keel, the rocking in
the sand,

I see the sailor kit, the canvas bag, the great box bound
with brass,

I scan the face all berry-brown and bearded—the stout-
strong frame,
Dress'd in its russet suit of good Scotch cloth:

(Then what the told-out story of those twenty years? what
of the future?)
